The light sibling (centered-modal--light-1280.png) holds: white on deep blue, about rgb(8,65,234), measures about 7:1. Only dark mode breaks. Source: /home/user/veneer/src/styles/_tokens.scss sets $dark 'primary' to oklch(0.7 0.15 233). /home/user/veneer/src/styles/components/_button.scss, in the `@each $role in tokens.$roles` loop, hard-codes the label as `$foreground: var(--vn-palette-white-base)` for every role except `light`. That label does not change when the primary fill retunes for dark mode.
findings.expected: Bootstrap 5.3.8 picks a button's label colour for its fill. node_modules/bootstrap/scss/_buttons.scss: `@each $color, $value in $theme-colors { .btn-#{$color} { @include button-variant($value, $value, ...) } }`. mixins/_buttons.scss: `button-variant` defaults `$color: color-contrast($background)`, which picks the label that reaches `$min-contrast-ratio: 4.5`. For a fill near rgb(0,172,236), color-contrast returns black, at about 8:1. Bootstrap also leaves .btn-primary unchanged in dark mode: #0d6efd with a white label. Veneer's dark primary retune is deliberate (_tokens.scss comment: "Only the primary fill retunes"). Right looks like this: the label in the dark `.btn-primary` rules uses a dark foreground (for example `--vn-palette-black-base`, or a token with a dark value) whenever the dark fill is light. That brings the dark variant to the same 4.5:1 floor the light variant already meets. Referral: this defect sits in the button component, outside the modal source, and shows in every dark modal footer.

findings.region: Seventh alert, 'The light notice.' (around y 426-480)
findings.seen: The alert has no visible border and no visible fill against the white page. Its text is a pale gray (roughly #adb5bd), so the notice reads as faded placeholder text with contrast far under the other roles.
findings.expected: Bootstrap 5.3.8 _alert.scss `.alert-#{$state}` sets --bs-alert-color: var(--bs-light-text-emphasis), --bs-alert-bg: var(--bs-light-bg-subtle), and --bs-alert-border-color: var(--bs-light-border-subtle). _variables.scss sets $light-text-emphasis: $gray-700 (#495057), $light-bg-subtle: mix($gray-100, $white) (#fcfcfd), and $light-border-subtle: $gray-200 (#e9ecef). The result is dark-gray readable text inside a visible light-gray outline. The cause is in Veneer's src/styles/_mixins.scss `role-each` mixin. It derives every role's emphasis as `color-mix(in oklab, {fill} 70%, body text)` and its border as `{fill} 35%` over the white anchor. With the #f8f9fa light fill, the emphasis mixes to a pale gray and the border mixes to near-white. Bootstrap does not derive the light role's tiers from its fill. It pins them to fixed grays.

findings.region: Last alert, 'The dark notice.' (around y 497-551)
findings.seen: The fill is almost the page canvas and the border is barely visible. The text is a dim gray (roughly #4a5058) on a near-black surface, so the notice is close to unreadable. It is the faintest alert in the stack.
findings.expected: _variables-dark.scss sets $dark-text-emphasis-dark: $gray-300 (#dee2e6), $dark-bg-subtle-dark: mix($gray-800, $black) (#1a1d20), and $dark-border-subtle-dark: $gray-800 (#343a40). _alert.scss `.alert-#{$state}` reads those through --bs-dark-text-emphasis, --bs-dark-bg-subtle, and --bs-dark-border-subtle. The result is light-gray text in a visible #343a40 outline. Veneer's `role-each` mixin (src/styles/_mixins.scss) mixes the #212529 dark fill 70% into the body text for emphasis, 15% into the canvas for the fill, and 50% into the anchor for the border. For this role those mixes collapse toward the canvas.

findings.region: Last alert, 'The dark notice.'

findings.expected: _variables.scss sets $dark-bg-subtle: $gray-400 (#ced4da), $dark-text-emphasis: $gray-700 (#495057), and $dark-border-subtle: $gray-500 (#adb5bd). Bootstrap's dark alert therefore has a darker gray fill with mid-gray text. Veneer's fill is lighter and its text darker, because the `role-each` mix replaces Bootstrap's fixed grays.
